key_insight: AgentSkillOS introduces a principled two-stage framework that organizes large collections of agent skills into a recursive capability tree and then retrieves and orchestrates those skills to solve tasks at ecosystem scale, enabling systematic discovery and benchmarking.
problem_solved: How to efficiently discover, select, compose, manage, and evaluate a rapidly growing ecosystem of agent skills so practitioners can scale reuse and reliably solve diverse tasks.
method: Manage Skills: recursively categorize skills into a hierarchical capability tree (node-level categorization) for efficient discovery and navigation.
Solve Tasks: retrieve relevant skills from the tree and orchestrate/compose them into executable plans to solve incoming tasks.
Ecosystem management & benchmarking: provide tools/metrics for automated evaluation, versioning, pruning, and comparative benchmarking of skills across the ecosystem.
impact: Makes large-scale agent skill collections practical to use and maintain — improving skill reuse, reducing manual curation, and enabling reproducible evaluation of agent capabilities across tasks.
visual_elements: Capability tree diagram showing recursive node-level categorization of skills
Pipeline flowchart: Manage Skills → Retrieve → Orchestrate/Compose → Execute → Evaluate
Sankey or bipartite mapping showing task-to-skill retrieval and composition paths
Benchmark dashboard/leaderboard heatmap visualizing skill performance, coverage, and lifecycle (add/update/prune)
paper_title: Organizing, Orchestrating, and Benchmarking Agent Skills at Ecosystem Scale
paper_authors: Hao Li, Chunjiang Mu, Jianhao Chen, Siyue Ren, Zhiyao Cui
